claims.text: An ML-trained surrogate can accurately represent ab initio free energies for both solid and fluid phases.
The surrogate can preserve anharmonic effects in both phases.
The surrogate can preserve electron–vibration effects in both phases.
Replacing explicit ab initio evaluations with the ML surrogate will reduce computational cost while preserving phase-free-energy and melting-property fidelity.
Representative solid and fluid configurations are available for elemental or binary systems near their phase transitions.
A limited set of ab initio free-energy data from both phases is sufficient to train the proposed interatomic potential.
The trained surrogate will be used within an enhanced-sampling free-energy protocol.
The proposed method is restricted to elemental and binary systems.
The proposed temperature domain extends from approximately 20% below to 30% above the nominal fusion temperature.
The ML potential learns the detailed interatomic force landscape.
Learning the force landscape enables the potential to capture vibrational entropy and anharmonicity.
Learning the force landscape enables the potential to capture electron–vibration coupling.
Periodic validation and correction against ab initio data will retain the accuracy of free-energy and entropy estimates.
The workflow will achieve phase-free-energy errors within approximately 5% relative to explicit AIMD.
The workflow will predict fusion temperatures within a 2% error margin.
The workflow will reduce computational time by at least one order of magnitude relative to full AIMD.
The workflow will be two to three times faster than TOR-TILD for binary systems.
Applicability to multicomponent high-entropy systems is uncertain because capturing all relevant entropy contributions is more complex.
